# Tool reference

<!-- Generated by .github/scripts/tool-reference.py; edit its reviewed JSON notes, then regenerate. -->

This reference describes the shared MCP and CLI tool interface. Parameter names,
types, required fields and schema limits come from the executable's tool catalog.
Defaults, response descriptions and behavioral restrictions are reviewed against
the implementation. Google can impose additional API, coverage and quota limits.

## Calling conventions

Examples under each tool are MCP **argument objects**. Pass that object to the
host's matching tool. For raw MCP `tools/call`, put the tool name in `name` and
the object in `arguments`. Hosts may prefix tool names. With the CLI, use
`mcp-gmap-rs call TOOL --args JSON` or the equivalent command/flags shown below.

Only top-level parameters have CLI flags. Supply nested objects and arrays as
JSON. Bare boolean flags mean true; `--flag false` sets false. Unknown top-level properties
are rejected. Native API body objects accept Google's documented fields, which Google validates. Inspect an installed version with `tools` or `schema TOOL` before
assuming it supports this release's complete catalog.

Language-aware calls use the configured Google language. API-key/OAuth selection is process
configuration, never a tool parameter. Exact `latitude,longitude` strings used
as route waypoints are preserved; names may require Geocoding and Places fallback.

All calls can be billable and share configured attempt budgets, deadlines and
retries. Composite and matrix results may contain per-item errors on an otherwise
successful call. Inspect those fields. Preserve Google links, review/photo authors
and AI-summary disclosures with returned content. Examples are illustrative, not
promises of current results or geographic coverage.

## maps_geocode

Convert an address or landmark to coordinates.

Resolve an address or landmark to the first Geocoding match. Use this to obtain reusable coordinates and a place ID; it does not validate postal deliverability.

**CLI command:** `geocode`. **Google access:** API key required in this implementation.

### Parameters

| Parameter / CLI flag | Type and schema limits | Required | Default when omitted | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `address` / `--address` | string; at least 1 character(s) | Yes | — | Address, city or landmark to geocode. |

### Behavior and restrictions

- No match is a tool error, not an empty successful location.
- This direct tool uses Geocoding v3; Places fallback is used by location-resolving composites, not by this call.

### Result

An object with `location.lat`, `location.lng`, `formatted_address` and `place_id`. Only the first result is returned.

### Example

MCP arguments:

```json
{
  "address": "Eiffel Tower, Paris, France"
}
```

Equivalent CLI call:

```sh
mcp-gmap-rs call maps_geocode --args '{"address":"Eiffel Tower, Paris, France"}'
```

## maps_validate_address

Validate and standardize a postal address; returns Google's verdict, corrections, components and geocode. A verdict is evidence, not a delivery guarantee.

Validate postal components and return corrections, the standardized address and Google’s verdict. Keep the verdict and unresolved components visible to the caller.

**CLI command:** `validate-address`. **Google access:** API key or OAuth for the main API.

### Parameters

| Parameter / CLI flag | Type and schema limits | Required | Default when omitted | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `addressLines` / `--address-lines` | array of string; 1–10 items; each item at least 1 character(s) | Yes | — | One or more postal-address lines, in order. |
| `administrativeArea` / `--administrative-area` | string; at least 1 character(s) | No | Not supplied | State, province or corresponding administrative area. |
| `enableUspsCass` / `--enable-usps-cass` | boolean | No | false | Request USPS CASS processing; this implementation requires regionCode US or PR when true. |
| `locality` / `--locality` | string; at least 1 character(s) | No | Not supplied | City or locality. |
| `postalCode` / `--postal-code` | string; at least 1 character(s) | No | Not supplied | Postal/ZIP code. |
| `regionCode` / `--region-code` | string; pattern: `^[A-Z]{2}$` | No | Not supplied; Google may infer it | Two-letter uppercase country/region code; recommended to disambiguate the address. |
| `sessionToken` / `--session-token` | string; at least 1 character(s) | No | No session token; Google bills outside an Autocomplete session | Same-project Autocomplete (New) session token. Reuse the prediction token in this concluding request; create a fresh token for the next session. |

### Behavior and restrictions

- A validation verdict is not a delivery guarantee.
- Region/API coverage varies. This tool does not submit validation feedback or automatically accept corrections.

### Result

The complete validation response, typically including `result.verdict`, `result.address`, `result.geocode` and `responseId`; Google may omit unavailable fields.

### Example

MCP arguments:

```json
{
  "addressLines": [
    "5 Avenue Anatole France"
  ],
  "regionCode": "FR",
  "locality": "Paris",
  "postalCode": "75007"
}
```

Equivalent CLI call:

```sh
mcp-gmap-rs call maps_validate_address --args '{"addressLines":["5 Avenue Anatole France"],"regionCode":"FR","locality":"Paris","postalCode":"75007"}'
```

## maps_pollen

Get 1-5 days of pollen forecasts, indices and health recommendations for exact coordinates. Coverage varies by location and season.

Retrieve a short daily pollen forecast for exact coordinates. The response preserves pollen types, indices, plant information and provider recommendations.

**CLI command:** `pollen`. **Google access:** API key required in this implementation.

### Parameters

| Parameter / CLI flag | Type and schema limits | Required | Default when omitted | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `days` / `--days` | integer; 1–5 | No | 1 | Number of daily forecast records to request. |
| `latitude` / `--latitude` | number; -90.0–90.0 | Yes | — | WGS84 latitude in decimal degrees; north is positive. |
| `longitude` / `--longitude` | number; -180.0–180.0 | Yes | — | WGS84 longitude in decimal degrees; east is positive. |
| `plantsDescription` / `--plants-description` | boolean | No | false | Include detailed plant descriptions and related information when available. |

### Behavior and restrictions

- Requests use a page size of 5, sufficient for this tool’s maximum five-day request; no additional pages are fetched automatically.
- Availability depends on location, season and Google coverage.

### Result

The original Pollen response, including `regionCode`, `dailyInfo` and any `nextPageToken`. Each day can include pollen-type and plant information.

### Example

MCP arguments:

```json
{
  "latitude": 48.8584,
  "longitude": 2.2945,
  "days": 3,
  "plantsDescription": false
}
```

Equivalent CLI call:

```sh
mcp-gmap-rs call maps_pollen --args '{"latitude":48.8584,"longitude":2.2945,"days":3,"plantsDescription":false}'
```

## maps_area_insights

Count places within a circle, region or polygon using Places Aggregate. Optional place IDs are available only for counts of 100 or less; no automatic details requests.

Count matching places in a circle, region or polygon with Places Aggregate. This is an aggregate query rather than a count of a limited Places search page.

**CLI command:** `area-insights`. **Google access:** API key or OAuth for the main API.

### Parameters

| Parameter / CLI flag | Type and schema limits | Required | Default when omitted | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `area` / `--area` | object | Yes | — | Exactly one of circle, region or customArea. |
| `area.circle` | object | No | Not supplied | Circular area; mutually exclusive with region/customArea. |
| `area.circle.latLng` | object | When parent is supplied | — | Circle center as exact coordinates. |
| `area.circle.latLng.latitude` | number; -90.0–90.0 | When parent is supplied | — | WGS84 latitude in decimal degrees; north is positive. |
| `area.circle.latLng.longitude` | number; -180.0–180.0 | When parent is supplied | — | WGS84 longitude in decimal degrees; east is positive. |
| `area.circle.radius` | integer; 23–50000 | When parent is supplied | — | Circle radius in metres. |
| `area.customArea` | object | No | Not supplied | Custom polygon area; mutually exclusive with circle/region. |
| `area.customArea.polygon` | object | When parent is supplied | — | Polygon boundary. |
| `area.customArea.polygon.coordinates` | array of object; 4–1000 items | When parent is supplied | — | Ordered ring of coordinate objects; first and last coordinates must match. |
| `area.customArea.polygon.coordinates[].latitude` | number; -90.0–90.0 | When parent is supplied | — | WGS84 latitude in decimal degrees; north is positive. |
| `area.customArea.polygon.coordinates[].longitude` | number; -180.0–180.0 | When parent is supplied | — | WGS84 longitude in decimal degrees; east is positive. |
| `area.region` | object | No | Not supplied | An administrative/geographic region identified by a Google place resource. |
| `area.region.place` | string; pattern: `^places/[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$` | When parent is supplied | — | Region resource in places/PLACE_ID format, not a free-form region name. |
| `excludedTypes` / `--excluded-types` | array of string; 1–50 items; each item at least 1 character(s) | No | No excluded-type filter | Google place types to exclude. |
| `includePlaces` / `--include-places` | boolean | No | false | Request matching place resource IDs in addition to the count. |
| `includedTypes` / `--included-types` | array of string; 1–50 items; each item at least 1 character(s) | Yes | — | Google place types to include, such as restaurant or cafe. |
| `maxRating` / `--max-rating` | number; 1.0–5.0 | No | No upper rating filter | Inclusive upper rating bound. |
| `minRating` / `--min-rating` | number; 1.0–5.0 | No | No lower rating filter | Inclusive lower rating bound; cannot exceed maxRating. |
| `operatingStatus` / `--operating-status` | array of string; 1–3 items; values: `OPERATING_STATUS_OPERATIONAL`, `OPERATING_STATUS_PERMANENTLY_CLOSED`, `OPERATING_STATUS_TEMPORARILY_CLOSED` | No | Google defaults to operational places | Allowed operating states. |
| `priceLevels` / `--price-levels` | array of string; 1–5 items; values: `PRICE_LEVEL_FREE`, `PRICE_LEVEL_INEXPENSIVE`, `PRICE_LEVEL_MODERATE`, `PRICE_LEVEL_EXPENSIVE`, `PRICE_LEVEL_VERY_EXPENSIVE` | No | All price levels | Allowed price levels. |

### Behavior and restrictions

- Supply exactly one area form. Nested objects are JSON values on the CLI; their child parameters do not have independent flags.
- Polygon rings must be closed. Google also checks polygon geometry, supported types, area and coverage.
- Place IDs are available only for counts of 100 or less. The tool does not automatically request Place Details.

### Result

Google’s response with `count` (normally an int64 string) and optional `placeInsights[].place` resources when IDs were requested and available.

### Example

MCP arguments:

```json
{
  "area": {
    "circle": {
      "latLng": {
        "latitude": 48.8584,
        "longitude": 2.2945
      },
      "radius": 500
    }
  },
  "includedTypes": [
    "restaurant"
  ],
  "minRating": 4
}
```

Equivalent CLI call:

```sh
mcp-gmap-rs call maps_area_insights --args '{"area":{"circle":{"latLng":{"latitude":48.8584,"longitude":2.2945},"radius":500}},"includedTypes":["restaurant"],"minRating":4}'
```

## maps_snap_to_roads

Snap an ordered GPS path of 2-100 points to roads. Keep consecutive points within about 300 metres for good results. Optional interpolation adds road geometry.

Match an ordered GPS trace to the most likely road geometry. Use Nearest Roads for independent points rather than a travelled path.

**CLI command:** `snap-to-roads`. **Google access:** API key required in this implementation.

### Parameters

| Parameter / CLI flag | Type and schema limits | Required | Default when omitted | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `interpolate` / `--interpolate` | boolean | No | false | Add intermediate road geometry between supplied points. |
| `path` / `--path` | array of object; 2–100 items | Yes | — | GPS coordinate objects in travel order. |
| `path[].latitude` | number; -90.0–90.0 | When parent is supplied | — | WGS84 latitude in decimal degrees; north is positive. |
| `path[].longitude` | number; -180.0–180.0 | When parent is supplied | — | WGS84 longitude in decimal degrees; east is positive. |

### Behavior and restrictions

- Consecutive input points should be within about 300 metres for good matching.
- Interpolated points may not have an originalIndex. Speed limits are not requested by this tool.

### Result

The original Roads response, including `snappedPoints` and any `warningMessage`. Points preserve road `placeId`, `location` and `originalIndex` when provided.

### Example

MCP arguments:

```json
{
  "path": [
    {
      "latitude": -35.27801,
      "longitude": 149.12958
    },
    {
      "latitude": -35.28032,
      "longitude": 149.12907
    }
  ],
  "interpolate": true
}
```

Equivalent CLI call:

```sh
mcp-gmap-rs call maps_snap_to_roads --args '{"path":[{"latitude":-35.27801,"longitude":149.12958},{"latitude":-35.28032,"longitude":149.12907}],"interpolate":true}'
```

## maps_nearest_roads

Find the nearest road segments for 1-100 independent GPS points; preserves Google's originalIndex and road place IDs.

Find nearby road segments for independent GPS points without interpreting them as one continuous trace.

**CLI command:** `nearest-roads`. **Google access:** API key required in this implementation.

### Parameters

| Parameter / CLI flag | Type and schema limits | Required | Default when omitted | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `points` / `--points` | array of object; 1–100 items | Yes | — | Independent coordinate objects to match. |
| `points[].latitude` | number; -90.0–90.0 | When parent is supplied | — | WGS84 latitude in decimal degrees; north is positive. |
| `points[].longitude` | number; -180.0–180.0 | When parent is supplied | — | WGS84 longitude in decimal degrees; east is positive. |

### Behavior and restrictions

- A point can match more than one road segment; retain originalIndex rather than assuming one output per input.
- Speed limits are not requested by this tool.

### Result

The original Roads response with `snappedPoints`, road `placeId`, `location` and `originalIndex` mapping back to input points.

### Example

MCP arguments:

```json
{
  "points": [
    {
      "latitude": -35.27801,
      "longitude": 149.12958
    },
    {
      "latitude": -35.28032,
      "longitude": 149.12907
    }
  ]
}
```

Equivalent CLI call:

```sh
mcp-gmap-rs call maps_nearest_roads --args '{"points":[{"latitude":-35.27801,"longitude":149.12958},{"latitude":-35.28032,"longitude":149.12907}]}'
```

## maps_reverse_geocode

Convert coordinates to a street address.

Convert exact coordinates to the first reverse-Geocoding result. Use the result’s components when a formatted address alone is insufficient.

**CLI command:** `reverse-geocode`. **Google access:** API key required in this implementation.

### Parameters

| Parameter / CLI flag | Type and schema limits | Required | Default when omitted | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `latitude` / `--latitude` | number; -90.0–90.0 | Yes | — | WGS84 latitude in decimal degrees; north is positive. |
| `longitude` / `--longitude` | number; -180.0–180.0 | Yes | — | WGS84 longitude in decimal degrees; east is positive. |

### Behavior and restrictions

- Only the first result is returned. No match is a tool error.

### Result

The first native Geocoding result, including `formatted_address`, `address_components`, `geometry` and `place_id` when available.

### Example

MCP arguments:

```json
{
  "latitude": 48.8584,
  "longitude": 2.2945
}
```

Equivalent CLI call:

```sh
mcp-gmap-rs call maps_reverse_geocode --args '{"latitude":48.8584,"longitude":2.2945}'
```

## maps_search_places

Search Places (New) by text with optional location and rating filters.

Search Places (New) by text and optional location/rating/type filters. Use returned IDs for selective detail requests.

**CLI command:** `search-places`. **Google access:** API key or OAuth for the main API.

### Parameters

| Parameter / CLI flag | Type and schema limits | Required | Default when omitted | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `includedType` / `--included-type` | string; at least 1 character(s) | No | No type filter | Google place type, such as cafe. |
| `locationBias` / `--location-bias` | object | No | No location bias | Optional circular search bias; a bias is not a hard geographic restriction. |
| `locationBias.latitude` | number; -90.0–90.0 | When parent is supplied | — | WGS84 latitude in decimal degrees; north is positive. |
| `locationBias.longitude` | number; -180.0–180.0 | When parent is supplied | — | WGS84 longitude in decimal degrees; east is positive. |
| `locationBias.radius` | number; 0.1–50000.0 | No | 5000 | Bias radius in metres. |
| `minRating` / `--min-rating` | number; 0.0–5.0 | No | No rating filter | Minimum user rating requested from Google. |
| `openNow` / `--open-now` | boolean | No | No opening-status restriction | Restrict to places currently open when true. |
| `query` / `--query` | string; at least 1 character(s) | Yes | — | Natural-language place query. |

### Behavior and restrictions

- This tool requests one page of 20 results and does not return or automatically follow a page token.
- Missing opening/rating data depends on Google coverage; do not infer an exhaustive inventory from this search.

### Result

An array of up to 20 Google Place objects with selected search fields, Maps/source links and attribution metadata.

### Example

MCP arguments:

```json
{
  "query": "coffee near Gare de Lyon, Paris",
  "openNow": true,
  "minRating": 4
}
```

Equivalent CLI call:

```sh
mcp-gmap-rs call maps_search_places --args '{"query":"coffee near Gare de Lyon, Paris","openNow":true,"minRating":4}'
```

## maps_search_nearby

Find places around an address or exact coordinate pair, filtered by type, rating, and opening status.

Find places inside a bounded radius around a resolved center. Unlike Text Search, this uses a hard circular location restriction.

**CLI command:** `search-nearby`. **Google access:** Places accepts API key or OAuth. Address/landmark centers also need an API key for Geocoding resolution.

### Parameters

| Parameter / CLI flag | Type and schema limits | Required | Default when omitted | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `center` / `--center` | object | Yes | — | Center input and the indicator describing how to interpret it. |
| `center.isCoordinates` | boolean | No | false | Treat value as exact coordinates without geocoding. |
| `center.value` | string; at least 1 character(s) | When parent is supplied | — | Address/landmark, or a latitude,longitude string when isCoordinates is true. |
| `keyword` / `--keyword` | string; at least 1 character(s) | No | No type filter | A Google place type passed as includedTypes, such as cafe; not an arbitrary text keyword. |
| `minRating` / `--min-rating` | number; 0.0–5.0 | No | No rating filter | Minimum rating applied locally to the returned places. |
| `openNow` / `--open-now` | boolean | No | false | Keep only results whose currentOpeningHours.openNow is true. |
| `radius` / `--radius` | number; 0.1–50000.0 | No | 1000 | Search radius in metres. |

### Behavior and restrictions

- When filtering, missing opening status does not count as open and missing rating is treated as 0.
- Address centers require location resolution; coordinates avoid that extra call.

### Result

An array of up to 20 selected Place objects. Local opening/rating filters can reduce the array further.

### Example

MCP arguments:

```json
{
  "center": {
    "value": "48.8584,2.2945",
    "isCoordinates": true
  },
  "keyword": "cafe",
  "radius": 500
}
```

Equivalent CLI call:

```sh
mcp-gmap-rs call maps_search_nearby --args '{"center":{"value":"48.8584,2.2945","isCoordinates":true},"keyword":"cafe","radius":500}'
```

## maps_place_details

Get full place details, reviews and attribution. Optional photo URLs retain author attribution. Display source/disclosure metadata alongside content.

Expand a known place ID into selected details, reviews and optional photo URLs. Preserve author/source information and any AI disclosure text.

**CLI command:** `place-details`. **Google access:** API key or OAuth for the main API.

### Parameters

| Parameter / CLI flag | Type and schema limits | Required | Default when omitted | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `maxPhotos` / `--max-photos` | integer; 0–10 | No | 0 | Maximum photo-media URL lookups to perform. |
| `placeId` / `--place-id` | string; at least 1 character(s) | Yes | — | Google place ID, optionally prefixed with places/. |
| `sessionToken` / `--session-token` | string; at least 1 character(s) | No | No session token; Google bills outside an Autocomplete session | Same-project Autocomplete (New) session token. Reuse the prediction token in this concluding request; create a fresh token for the next session. |

### Behavior and restrictions

- Each selected photo can make an additional request; zero photos avoids those calls.
- The tool uses a fixed details field mask, not every possible Google Place field. Unavailable fields may be absent.

### Result

A native Google Place object for the requested field mask. When photos are requested, `photoUrls` carries media URLs plus photo-author attribution and source links.

### Example

MCP arguments:

```json
{
  "placeId": "ChIJLU7jZClu5kcR4PcOOO6p3I0",
  "maxPhotos": 1
}
```

Equivalent CLI call:

```sh
mcp-gmap-rs call maps_place_details --args '{"placeId":"ChIJLU7jZClu5kcR4PcOOO6p3I0","maxPhotos":1}'
```

## maps_directions

Get directions, route geometry, navigation instructions and travel duration.

Compute a route between two endpoints and expose both selected Google route data and normalized totals.

**CLI command:** `directions`. **Google access:** Routes/Places accept API key or OAuth. Named-location resolution also needs an API key for Geocoding; exact coordinate strings avoid that lookup.

### Parameters

| Parameter / CLI flag | Type and schema limits | Required | Default when omitted | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `arrival_time` / `--arrival-time` | string; at least 1 character(s) | No | Not supplied | Desired arrival as RFC 3339 with timezone; transit mode only. |
| `avoid_highways` / `--avoid-highways` | boolean | No | false | Avoid highways; true is supported only for driving. |
| `avoid_tolls` / `--avoid-tolls` | boolean | No | false | Avoid toll roads; true is supported only for driving. |
| `departure_time` / `--departure-time` | string; at least 1 character(s) | No | Not supplied | Departure instant as RFC 3339 including Z or an explicit UTC offset. |
| `destination` / `--destination` | string; at least 1 character(s) | Yes | — | Destination address/landmark or exact latitude,longitude string. |
| `mode` / `--mode` | string; values: `driving`, `walking`, `bicycling`, `transit` | No | driving | Travel mode. Driving uses traffic-aware routing. |
| `origin` / `--origin` | string; at least 1 character(s) | Yes | — | Origin address/landmark or exact latitude,longitude string. |
| `trafficSegments` / `--traffic-segments` | boolean | No | false | Boolean opt-in for driving only. Requests TRAFFIC_ON_POLYLINE with HIGH_QUALITY and ENCODED_POLYLINE geometry. Traffic on polylines triggers the higher-priced Compute Routes Enterprise SKU; leave false unless segment detail is needed. |

### Behavior and restrictions

- departure_time and arrival_time cannot both be supplied. arrival_time is accepted only for transit.
- Avoidance flags require driving. Google applies additional travel-mode/time/region restrictions.
- No available route is an explicit error.
- With trafficSegments=true, Routes supplies NORMAL, SLOW or TRAFFIC_JAM intervals. Normalized route and leg segments use the corresponding route or leg polyline, with independent point indices. Google intervals are [start,end); each segment geometry retains the shared end boundary vertex to cover the final edge. Missing or invalid coverage is reported explicitly rather than invented as normal traffic.
- segmentMetadata.retrievedAt is the local response-fetch time, not a provider traffic observation time; trafficObservedAt is null because Routes does not return it. roadCategory and speedLimit are null because this Routes response supplies neither. No implicit Roads API calls or client-side duration multipliers are applied; durations remain Google predictions.
- Traffic segments are optional and driving-only in this executable. This requests traffic-aware polylines and triggers Compute Routes Enterprise billing. [Traffic interval contract](https://developers.google.com/maps/documentation/routes/traffic_on_polylines); [current SKU triggers](https://developers.google.com/maps/billing-and-pricing/sku-details/routes).

### Result

An object containing `routes`, `summary`, `total_distance` (value in metres), `total_duration` (value in seconds) and optional optimization indices. Route entries contain selected legs, steps, polyline and warnings. When trafficSegments is true, route and leg results additionally include normalized segments and segmentMetadata.

### Example

MCP arguments:

```json
{
  "origin": "48.8584,2.2945",
  "destination": "48.8606,2.3376",
  "mode": "walking"
}
```

Equivalent CLI call:

```sh
mcp-gmap-rs call maps_directions --args '{"origin":"48.8584,2.2945","destination":"48.8606,2.3376","mode":"walking"}'
```

## maps_distance_matrix

Compute travel distances and durations for multiple origins and destinations.

Compare travel distance and duration for every origin/destination pair. Check individual cells and errors rather than treating a successful response as complete.

**CLI command:** `distance-matrix`. **Google access:** API key or OAuth for the main API.

### Parameters

| Parameter / CLI flag | Type and schema limits | Required | Default when omitted | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `avoid_highways` / `--avoid-highways` | boolean | No | false | Avoid highways; true is supported only for driving. |
| `avoid_tolls` / `--avoid-tolls` | boolean | No | false | Avoid toll roads; true is supported only for driving. |
| `departure_time` / `--departure-time` | string; at least 1 character(s) | No | Not supplied | Departure instant as RFC 3339 including Z or an explicit UTC offset. |
| `destinations` / `--destinations` | array of string; 1–50 items; each item at least 1 character(s) | Yes | — | Destination strings: addresses or exact latitude,longitude pairs. |
| `mode` / `--mode` | string; values: `driving`, `walking`, `bicycling`, `transit` | No | driving | Travel mode. Driving uses traffic-aware routing. |
| `origins` / `--origins` | array of string; 1–50 items; each item at least 1 character(s) | Yes | — | Origin strings: addresses or exact latitude,longitude pairs. |

### Behavior and restrictions

- At most 625 origin × destination pairs; transit is limited to 100 pairs.
- At most 50 non-coordinate origin/destination strings in total. Per-array schema limits do not override these combined limits.
- Toll/highway avoidance applies only to driving. This tool does not expose arrival_time.
- A single matrix HTTP request may bill multiple elements.

### Result

An object with `origin_addresses`, `destination_addresses`, row-major `distances` and `durations`, and an `errors` array. Successful cell values are metres/seconds; failed or missing cells remain null.

### Example

MCP arguments:

```json
{
  "origins": [
    "48.8584,2.2945"
  ],
  "destinations": [
    "48.8606,2.3376",
    "48.8530,2.3499"
  ],
  "mode": "walking"
}
```

Equivalent CLI call:

```sh
mcp-gmap-rs call maps_distance_matrix --args '{"origins":["48.8584,2.2945"],"destinations":["48.8606,2.3376","48.8530,2.3499"],"mode":"walking"}'
```

## maps_timezone

Get timezone, UTC/DST offsets and local time. timestamp is Unix milliseconds.

Resolve timezone identity and UTC/DST offsets at an instant, then derive a local timestamp.

**CLI command:** `timezone`. **Google access:** API key required in this implementation.

### Parameters

| Parameter / CLI flag | Type and schema limits | Required | Default when omitted | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `latitude` / `--latitude` | number; -90.0–90.0 | Yes | — | WGS84 latitude in decimal degrees; north is positive. |
| `longitude` / `--longitude` | number; -180.0–180.0 | Yes | — | WGS84 longitude in decimal degrees; east is positive. |
| `timestamp` / `--timestamp` | integer; 0–253402300799999 | No | Current UTC time in milliseconds | Unix epoch milliseconds, not seconds. |

### Behavior and restrictions

- The request converts milliseconds to whole seconds; sub-second precision is not preserved.
- Local time uses the returned raw and DST offsets for the requested instant.

### Result

Timezone response fields such as `timeZoneId`, `timeZoneName`, `rawOffset` and `dstOffset` in seconds, plus derived `localTime` in RFC 3339 format.

### Example

MCP arguments:

```json
{
  "latitude": 48.8584,
  "longitude": 2.2945,
  "timestamp": 1793448000000
}
```

Equivalent CLI call:

```sh
mcp-gmap-rs call maps_timezone --args '{"latitude":48.8584,"longitude":2.2945,"timestamp":1793448000000}'
```

## maps_static_map

Fetch a PNG map with markers and paths. MCP returns an inline image; CLI returns base64 JSON or writes --output.

Render a PNG map with optional markers and path specifications.

**CLI command:** `static-map`. **Google access:** API key required in this implementation.

### Parameters

| Parameter / CLI flag | Type and schema limits | Required | Default when omitted | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `center` / `--center` | string; at least 1 character(s) | No | Not supplied | Center as an address or latitude,longitude string. |
| `maptype` / `--maptype` | string; values: `roadmap`, `satellite`, `terrain`, `hybrid` | No | roadmap | Base map style. |
| `markers` / `--markers` | array of string; 1–100 items; each item at least 1 character(s) | No | No markers | Repeated Google Static Maps marker specifications, e.g. color:red\|48.8584,2.2945. |
| `path` / `--path` | array of string; 1–100 items; each item at least 1 character(s) | No | No paths | Repeated Google Static Maps path specifications, e.g. color:blue\|48.8584,2.2945\|48.8606,2.3376. |
| `size` / `--size` | string; pattern: `^[1-9][0-9]{0,2}x[1-9][0-9]{0,2}$` | No | 600x400 | Pixel dimensions WIDTHxHEIGHT; runtime limits each dimension to 1–640. |
| `zoom` / `--zoom` | integer; 0–21 | No | Omitted; Google chooses or infers it | Explicit zoom level. |

### Behavior and restrictions

- At least one of center, markers or path is required.
- The complete request URL must fit within 16,384 characters. The schema’s size pattern is broader than the runtime’s 640-pixel bound.
- Marker/path styling follows Google Static Maps syntax. Google attribution remains in the rendered image.

### Result

MCP returns inline image/png content. CLI returns `{mimeType,base64}` JSON, or raw PNG bytes when --output is supplied.

### Example

MCP arguments:

```json
{
  "center": "48.8584,2.2945",
  "zoom": 14,
  "size": "320x240",
  "markers": [
    "color:red|48.8584,2.2945"
  ]
}
```

Equivalent CLI call:

```sh
mcp-gmap-rs call maps_static_map --args '{"center":"48.8584,2.2945","zoom":14,"size":"320x240","markers":["color:red|48.8584,2.2945"]}'
```

Resolve a location and explore categories with details for top results. Use specific landmarks for trip planning.

## maps_plan_route

Plan a route through 2-27 stops. Optimize 2-25 intermediate stops, except transit. Exact coordinates are preserved.

Plan a single route through ordered stops, optionally asking Google to reorder intermediate stops while keeping the endpoints fixed.

**CLI command:** `plan-route`. **Google access:** Routes/Places accept API key or OAuth. Named-location resolution also needs an API key for Geocoding; exact coordinate strings avoid that lookup.

### Parameters

| Parameter / CLI flag | Type and schema limits | Required | Default when omitted | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `avoid_highways` / `--avoid-highways` | boolean | No | false | Avoid highways; true is supported only for driving. |
| `avoid_tolls` / `--avoid-tolls` | boolean | No | false | Avoid toll roads; true is supported only for driving. |
| `departure_time` / `--departure-time` | string; at least 1 character(s) | No | Not supplied | Departure instant as RFC 3339 including Z or an explicit UTC offset. |
| `mode` / `--mode` | string; values: `driving`, `walking`, `bicycling`, `transit` | No | driving | Travel mode. Driving uses traffic-aware routing. |
| `optimize` / `--optimize` | boolean | No | true, subject to those conditions | Request intermediate-stop optimization when more than three total stops and mode is not transit. |
| `stops` / `--stops` | array of string; 2–27 items; each item at least 1 character(s) | Yes | — | Ordered addresses/landmarks or exact latitude,longitude strings; first/last stay endpoints. |
| `trafficSegments` / `--traffic-segments` | boolean | No | false | Boolean opt-in for driving only. Requests TRAFFIC_ON_POLYLINE with HIGH_QUALITY and ENCODED_POLYLINE geometry. Traffic on polylines triggers the higher-priced Compute Routes Enterprise SKU; leave false unless segment detail is needed. |

### Behavior and restrictions

- Transit supports only two endpoints and no intermediate stops.
- Optimization takes effect only for four or more total stops (at least two intermediate stops).
- This optimizes stop order for one route, not vehicle/task assignment across a fleet.
- With trafficSegments=true, Routes supplies NORMAL, SLOW or TRAFFIC_JAM intervals. Normalized route and leg segments use the corresponding route or leg polyline, with independent point indices. Google intervals are [start,end); each segment geometry retains the shared end boundary vertex to cover the final edge. Missing or invalid coverage is reported explicitly rather than invented as normal traffic.
- segmentMetadata.retrievedAt is the local response-fetch time, not a provider traffic observation time; trafficObservedAt is null because Routes does not return it. roadCategory and speedLimit are null because this Routes response supplies neither. No implicit Roads API calls or client-side duration multipliers are applied; durations remain Google predictions.
- Traffic segments are optional and driving-only in this executable. This requests traffic-aware polylines and triggers Compute Routes Enterprise billing. [Traffic interval contract](https://developers.google.com/maps/documentation/routes/traffic_on_polylines); [current SKU triggers](https://developers.google.com/maps/billing-and-pricing/sku-details/routes).

### Result

An object with `mode`, effective `optimized`, ordered resolved `stops`, display `legs`, total_distance, total_duration, polyline and warnings. Leg durationSeconds is numeric seconds. When trafficSegments is true, route and leg results additionally include normalized segments and segmentMetadata.

### Example

MCP arguments:

```json
{
  "stops": [
    "48.8584,2.2945",
    "48.8606,2.3376",
    "48.8530,2.3499"
  ],
  "mode": "walking",
  "optimize": false
}
```

Equivalent CLI call:

```sh
mcp-gmap-rs call maps_plan_route --args '{"stops":["48.8584,2.2945","48.8606,2.3376","48.8530,2.3499"],"mode":"walking","optimize":false}'
```

Search and compare places with detailed information and optional driving distance from userLocation.
